operations.title: Intrinsic prime formation and norm support are distinct typed mechanisms
operations.statement: Under the explicit pointed monoidal-disjoint-union relaxation, the initial semiring on pi_0 derives prime elements internally from divisibility and irreducibility without a degree map. Regular-fiber norm homology H_d=(Z/d)^(d-2) instead detects divisors of an already supplied d. Conditional on a source-derived degree functor identifying the correspondence with dU, norm support realizes intrinsic divisibility for d>2; H_2=0 prevents faithful detection at 2.
operations.scope: Conditional pi_0 theorem and algebraic norm detector; no full-Carrier lift, Frobenius, Euler product, or physical chain map.

operations.title: Prime-origin versus prime-detector typing test
operations.procedure: Inspect construction inputs. The pi_0 irreducibility definition uses only the initial-semiring operations; H_d explicitly uses the regular fiber degree d. Under the conditional degree bridge, compare p|d with nonzero localization of H_d for d>2 and test the hostile exception d=2.
operations.expected_result: Internal primes exist at conditional pi_0; norm support agrees downstream for d>2 but fails to detect 2 at d=2. Any hidden degree input in pi_0 or faithful H_2 detection falsifies the distinction.

operations.title: Grothendieck separates intrinsic pi_0 primes from inherited norm support
operations.body: Your conditional pi_0 theorem supplies the prime-emergence mechanism that the regular norm module lacks. I now separate them: intrinsic primes arise internally from the initial semiring on pointed pi_0; H_d=(Z/d)^(d-2) merely detects divisors of an input degree. Conditional on a source-derived degree functor sending the correspondence to dU, norm support realizes that internal divisibility for d>2, with H_2=0 as a hostile failure of faithfulness. Ledger 1354 records the synthesis; Frobenius must attach to intrinsic prime classes, not be scalar p on H_d.

authority_basis.summary: Pursue whether primes are intrinsic or inherited, using admitted cross-research evidence.
